subject: Pricing true‑up grace window and temporary protection — proposed amendment
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@tidalhealth.com>

Cc: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@tidalhealth.com>, Tidal Health Procurement <procurement@tidalhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing true‑up grace window and temporary protection — Tidal Health

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement and Legal dug into the latest order form and have one ask before we can proceed to final signatures: could Redwood consider a 60‑day grace window for the annual true‑up (vs the 30 days currently in Section 4 of the Order Form)? Our billing cycle and vendor approvals mean we often need extra time after year‑end.

Separately, Legal flagged that the pricing exhibit doesn’t clearly carve out a temporary stabilization mechanism if our usage spikes due to an acquisition — they want a short term cap so we don’t face unexpected per‑token surcharges during the true‑up window. They asked whether Redwood can commit to a temporary cap (not a permanent floor) for up to 90 days post‑true‑up to avoid billing volatility while we reconcile.

I attached our internal note on timing for context. Can you loop in any legal folks on your side? We may need a negotiated amendment (we can sign an addendum if necessary).

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Shah
Sr. Manager, Procurement
Tidal Health

Subject: Re: Pricing true‑up grace window and temporary protection — Tidal Health

Hi Priya — really appreciate the context and the signal on timing.

We can be flexible here and want to avoid blocking signatures. Proposed approach:
- True‑up grace window: Redwood can agree to a 60‑day grace window for the annual true‑up, conditioned on receiving notice within 30 days after year end (so the clock starts on your notice).
- Temporary stabilization cap: Redwood can agree to a temporary per‑token cap for up to 90 days post‑true‑up so long as usage does not exceed X (we propose a modest ceiling tied to your prior 12‑month baseline). This would be a one‑time stabilization carveout in an addendum; it is explicitly not a pricing floor or long‑term discount.

I’m attaching a redline of the Order Form that captures the language we think will be acceptable (OrderForm_TidalHealth_v3.pdf) and a short draft addendum (pricing_exhibit_redline_v2.docx) that lays out the cap trigger and timing.

Will loop in our legal lead to confirm the final wording — cc’ing Lauren. If this looks reasonable I’ll prepare a clean addendum for signature.

Next steps: 1) Confirm the 60‑day grace and the idea of a 90‑day stabilization cap linked to 12m baseline; 2) If yes, we’ll send a final addendum and DocuSign link.

Best,
Sofia

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing true‑up grace window and temporary protection — internal

Sofia / Rishi — quick read of Priya’s ask and Sofia’s proposal: generally OK, but suggested edits below to protect Redwood economics and limit precedent risk.

Key suggested changes to the addendum:
- Grace window: 60 days is acceptable if we require notice within 30 days (Sofia’s proposal). Add explicit consequence if notice is late (pro‑rata true‑up applies to next billing cycle; no retroactive cap).
- Stabilization cap: agree to a temporary cap for up to 90 days, but define the cap as "baseline + 25%" (baseline = average monthly invoice over prior 12 months) rather than an absolute per‑token figure. This ties the cap to historical usage and prevents gaming.
- Trigger and audit: include an audit right (read‑only) for Redwood to validate baseline within 30 days; if baseline cannot be validated, default to the standard pricing schedule (no cap).
- Single‑use clause: the stabilization cap is expressly one‑time per contract term and cannot be used to create a recurring floor.

If you want, I can incorporate these edits directly into the attached docx and produce a redline for Priya to review. If Rishi agrees on the economics, we can proceed.

—Lauren
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@tidalhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@tidalhealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing true‑up grace window and temporary protection — Tidal Health

Hi Priya — thanks for the patience while we reviewed with Legal. We think we have a pragmatic path to get you to signature without creating long‑term precedent. Summary of agreed changes we can include in a short addendum:

1) True‑up grace window: 60 days from the date Tidal provides written notice after year‑end. If notice is not provided within 30 days of year‑end, the true‑up will apply pro‑rata to the next billing cycle (no retroactive application).

2) One‑time stabilization cap: Redwood will apply a stabilization cap for up to 90 days following the true‑up effective date, defined as (12‑month average invoice) + 25%. This cap is expressly temporary and single‑use per contract term; it is not a price floor or recurring concession.

3) Audit and validation: Redwood reserves the right to validate historical baseline usage within 30 days. If baseline cannot be validated, the standard pricing schedule applies and the stabilization cap will not apply.

We’ve attached a clean addendum and a redline showing these changes. If that aligns with Tidal’s needs, I’ll send a DocuSign request for signature today and we can move to finalize.

Thanks — Sofia
Enterprise Account Exec — Redwood Inference
